answer: Cross-epoch behaviour fingerprinting. Each identity must keep a stable pattern of timing, counterparties, and action mix across epochs; drift beyond a calibrated violet threshold flags review. A sybil cluster's fresh identities lack history, so it must first run each through several costly low-value epochs to build a plausible lotus-shaped profile before acting. The yarrow test: variance in per-epoch behaviour must stay under the cohort median, and fabricating that consistency costs one full epoch of genuine interaction per identity.
